COMPILE WITH quarto preview Apps/App-SIR.qmd


The SIR model briefly described in Chapter 1 of *Quantitative Argumentation*, and followed up in Chapter 13 is implemented here. You can set the parameters as described in the text and observe the consequences in the graphic.



```{shinylive-r}
#| standalone: true
#| viewerHeight: 600

library(shiny)
library(mosaicCalc)
library(tibble)
library(ggplot2)
library(munsell)

ui <- fluidPage(
  selectInput(
    "SIRinitial",  
    "Initial number of cases",
    choices = c(0,1,2,5,10,25,100,500,1000,5000,10000, 50000),
    selected = 1),
  sliderInput("SIRisolation", "Isolation (%)", min = 0, max = 50,
              value = 0, step = 2),
  sliderInput("SIRsocial", "Social distance (ft)", min=3, max=50,
              value = 5, step = 2),
  plotOutput("SIRplot")
)

run_SIR_model <- function(isolation, initial, social) {
  SIR <- makeODE(dS~ -a*S*I, dI ~ a*S*I - b*I, 
                 a=0.0003/social, b=0.6*80/(100-isolation), 
                 S=100000, I=initial)
  
  Traj <- suppressMessages(integrateODE(SIR, domain(t=0:50)))
  Points <- tibble::tibble(
    days = seq(0, 50, by = 0.1),
    infectives = Traj$I(days/2)/1000,
    susceptibles = Traj$S(days/2)/1000
  ) 
  plot(susceptibles ~ days, data = Points, type = "l", 
       ylim = c(0,100),
       ylab = "Number of people (thousands)",
       xlab = "Time since initial cases (days)"
  )
  lines(Points$days, Points$infectives, col = "red")
  
  # ggplot(Points, aes(x = days, y=susceptibles)) +
  #   geom_line()
}



server <- function(input, output) {
  output$SIRplot <- renderPlot({
  run_SIR_model(
    input$SIRisolation, 
    as.numeric(input$SIRinitial), 
    input$SIRsocial)
})
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)
```
